title: Tablet Stands and Clamp Arms for Video Calls and Bedside Use: What They Do, What They Cost
subtitle: A plain-English look at three ways to hold a tablet, what each costs, and what a stand cannot fix.
excerpt: A stand or clamp arm can take the tablet out of your hands, but it will not fix a weak connection or a dim room. Here are the two main styles, three posted-price options, and the measuring to do before you order.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Holding a tablet by hand through a video call can be awkward. The picture may wobble, and the family on the other end can end up looking at your ceiling or your chin.

A tablet stand or clamp arm takes the holding job off your hands. It keeps the screen in one place, whether you are at the kitchen table or in bed. It is a small accessory, but it has limits, and a few details are worth checking before you buy.
"Laptops or tablets with stands — not smartphones — are best for video calls." — AARP, "Adapting to Social Distancing with Video Chats" (2020 tips box)
That is a 2020 tip, and it is the only AARP source we draw on here, so treat it as general guidance rather than a rule.
There are two main styles. A desk stand sits on a flat surface like a table or counter and holds the tablet at an angle. It suits using the tablet in one spot.

A clamp arm grips the edge of something, such as a table or desk, and holds the tablet on a bendable or jointed arm. Macally's page describes using its clamp holder in bed, at a desk or on a kitchen table. Clamping to a bed frame or headboard has not been checked by independent testing, and a clamp there can slip or rattle. The seller's own claim that the arm will not be knocked off is not independent evidence.

Within each style, some stands lock in one position while others adjust. BestReviews notes that single-position stands cost less if you will not move the screen. Its advice for everyone else is direct: "If you'll need to move the screen at all, get a tablet stand that's adjustable."

items: Measure first. Check the thickness of the table edge or bed frame where a clamp will go, and measure your tablet with its case on. Clamps and holders only fit a certain range.
Think about stiff hands. The product pages do not say how easy the knobs or joints are to tighten. If grip strength is a concern, try one in a store or ask the seller before choosing.
Check the edges. BestReviews suggests watching for sharp metal edges that could scratch a tablet without a case.
Sharing the tablet? BestReviews advises metal stands if the tablet is shared.
Read the return policy and warranty, and factor in shipping. Some stores ship free only above a certain order total.
Check the fit. Make sure the listing names your kind of tablet, and confirm the item is in stock.

sections.content: Setting it up for a good call

A stand only holds the tablet. It will not fix weak Wi-Fi, a dim room, or a camera pointed the wrong way. AARP's tips cover framing and glare: point the camera slightly down, avoid backlit glare from windows, and use earbuds with a built-in mic for clearer voice.

As general common-sense caution rather than sourced advice, if you use a clamp arm near a bed, check now and then that it is still holding firmly. A stand is also not a replacement for the tablet itself. See our separate guide on choosing a simple tablet for video calls.

Macally's page lists two different clamp thicknesses (up to 2.5 inches in one place, 1.75 inches in another) and two different tablet size ranges (7 to 11 inches, and 8 inches or less). Measure your furniture edge and your tablet in its case, and confirm with the seller before ordering. The page also showed a message that the quantity selected exceeds current stock, so confirm availability. Macally ships free only on orders of $49 or more, so a single holder may add a shipping charge.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: A good stand can make the tablet easier to use, but only if it fits your tablet and your furniture. Measure carefully, think about whose hands will be adjusting it, and pick the simplest style that suits where you sit.

products.name: Tablet Holder with Strong Universal Clamp (White, Adjustable), SKU CLIPMOUNTW
products.blurb: A low-priced clamp holder with an adjustable 11-inch steel gooseneck arm, with a 2-year warranty and 30-day returns. The page gives conflicting clamp thickness and tablet size figures, and showed a stock message, so confirm both before ordering.

products.name: Rain Design mStand tabletplus Tablet Stand, Silver (Model 10053)
products.blurb: A silver anodized aluminum desktop stand listed for Apple iPad only, so owners of other tablets should not assume it fits. Its listing copy mentions an adjustable angle, but the product page gives few other specs.

products.name: Articulating Arm w/ Tall & Thick Adjustable Tablet Holder
products.blurb: A specialty positioning arm with two segments and three joints, a Super-Clamp, and a holder that fits tablets in thick foam cases. At $219 it costs far more than the $30 and $54 options and is not a typical gift; it suits someone with a specific need for a positioning arm. Phone support: 1-800-RJCooper.
